a:T782,## Symptom

In back-to-back `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app` runs on the SAME commit (branch `fix/chat-widget-deslop`, 5-iteration loop for #15886), the Her-minimal ratchet (#9950) flipped on one view:

- Iterations 1 and 4: **pass** (0 ratchet violations, `plugin-inbox-gui` clean).
- Iterations 2, 3, 5: **fail** with exactly one violation — `plugin-inbox-gui @ mobile-landscape: border/divider density regressed 97.22 > baselined 72.91 + 5% tolerance (76.56)`.

The magnitude (≈33% over baseline vs clean-pass on identical code) suggests the view renders **different content** across runs — e.g. a divider-heavy populated list vs a sparser/empty state — not measurement jitter. It fires only at `mobile-landscape`.

Cross-checks:
- Two same-day CI `aesthetic-audit` runs on sibling branches from the same develop base (PRs #15889, #15894) show `plugin-inbox-gui` with **zero** ratchet violations at all four viewports.
- The branch under test changes only chat-widget/bubble styling in `packages/ui` — `plugins/plugin-inbox/src` imports none of the changed components (verified by grep), so the flip is not diff-induced.

## Why it matters

A coin-flip ratchet failure on an unrelated view fails the whole audit run (the gate is unconditional), which poisons the 5-loop grind required for UI PRs and trains people to ignore real ratchet regressions.

## Suggested fix directions

- Make the inbox GUI's audit fixture data deterministic at capture time (whatever feeds it rows appears to vary — check clock-relative filtering or unseeded data in the mocked /api fixtures for the inbox view at landscape widths).
- Or have the ratchet retry/flag single-view flips (same view passing and failing across consecutive same-commit runs) as `needs-eyeball` instead of failing the run.

c:T2335,## Light Phone III voice pipeline — findings, fixes, and remaining work (cloud STT/TTS on stripped AOSP)

Tracking issue for the LP3 (Light Phone III) hybrid-cloud voice work. The LP3 is a 6 GB, Qualcomm Adreno 613, **stripped LightOS/AOSP** device: no Google speech-recognition service, no proprietary media codecs in the WebView, and it runs the on-device agent over a Unix socket rather than a TCP port. Those three gaps break every native voice assumption in the app, and each surfaced as a separate bug. This documents what we found, what we fixed, the architecture, and what's still open.

**Mode:** hybrid — the on-device agent runtime boots locally, but text inference is **direct Cerebras** (`gemma-4-31b`, OPENAI-compat passthrough), and voice is routed to **Eliza Cloud** (STT/TTS). Local on-device voice (Shaw's Kokoro + fused Gemma ASR) works but is ~10–16 s/turn on this CPU, so cloud is the pragmatic path.

---

### ✅ What works now
- **Text chat** — Cerebras `gemma-4-31b`, ~2–3 s, streams tokens (SSE).
- **Cloud STT** — `POST /api/asr/cloud` → Eliza Cloud **OpenAI Whisper**, ~1.8–2.4 s, accurate transcripts.
- **Mic capture** — the waveform/"talk" button now records via the WebView (getUserMedia) on the cloud path; **no native recognizer, no loop** (verified: 0 `Recognition error (5)`, mic `curActiveCount=1`).
- **Cloud TTS fetch** — `POST /api/tts/cloud` → 200, MP3 audio, ~2–2.8 s.
- **End-to-end pipeline fires**: speech → transcript → Gemma reply → TTS fetch. Confirmed live (agent replied "not much, just here and ready to help").

### ❌ The one remaining blocker: audio playback (no MP3 codec)
The cloud returns **MP3** (`audio/mpeg`, ElevenLabs `eleven_flash_v2_5`). LightOS's WebView **cannot decode MP3 by any path**:
- `AudioContext.decodeAudioData(mp3)` → throws `Unable to decode audio data`.
- `<audio>` element with an MP3 blob → `MediaError code 4` (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED).

So the reply is generated correctly but is **silent**. This is the single thing standing between "works" and "works with sound."

**Fix options (ranked):**
1. **Make the cloud TTS return WAV/PCM** for this client — WAV needs no codec and `decodeAudioData` handles it. There is currently **no `outputFormat`/`format` param** on `/voice/tts` (verified), so this needs a cloud-side option (or a Kokoro-cloud path that emits WAV). *Recommended.*
2. Ship a **WASM MP3 decoder** in the client for codec-less WebViews (heavier bundle).
3. Use **local Kokoro TTS** (returns WAV) — but it's slow on LP3 and the native voice lib got dropped in the APK rebuild (see below).

---

### 🐞 Bugs found + fixes (the saga)
Each of these was a distinct LP3-specific failure. Commits are local (not pushed).

1. **On-device agent chat-send 404** — the Android local-agent IPC bridge only served *plugin* routes (`runtime.routes`); core routes (`/api/conversations`, message stream, etc.) 404'd. Fixed by bridging the full server request handler through the IPC path. *(iOS/HTTP parity bug — genuinely upstream-worthy.)*

2. **On-device CPU voice via the bionic host** — the fused `libelizainference` can't be dlopen'd by the musl agent; runs in-app via JNI over a UDS. Vulkan backend **SIGSEGVs on Adreno 613** (Mali-only), so added an opt-in **CPU** path (`eliza:voice-cpu-host`). Proven: local Kokoro TTS 200/audio, fused ASR real transcript. KEY: `eliza_inference_create` is metadata-only — **voice never loads the 1.27 GB text model** (Shaw's lazy design). *Slow (~16 s) but works.*

3. **Native mic → infinite recognizer loop** — the app registers **itself** as the Android `RecognitionService`. On LP3 (no real recognizer), a native STT attempt hits `ElizaRecognitionService.onStartListening` → fires the `elizaos://voice` deep-link → `toggleHandsFree` → `startListening` → native again → **infinite loop** (`Recognition error: Client error (5)` every ~0.6 s). Broken by routing capture entirely to cloud (below).

4. **THE root cause — capture factory ignored the cloud preference** — `resolveBackendKind` (`voice-capture-factory.ts`) returned `"talkmode"` for **any** native platform **before** it ever checked `preferred === "eliza-cloud"`. So the hands-free capture (`useShellController.startCapture` → `createVoiceCapture`, a path entirely separate from `useVoiceChat.startListening`) **always** used the native recognizer and ignored the cloud setting. Fixed: an explicit `eliza-cloud`/`openai` ASR preference now wins over native talk-mode when WAV capture exists (undefined/local-inference still prefer native → other devices unchanged).

5. **Opt-in cloud voice plumbing** (`eliza:voice-cloud-tts`) — forces `cloudConnected`/`asrProvider` to cloud since the hybrid config never advertises cloud voice (`/api/cloud/status` returns `cloudVoiceProxyAvailable:false` because `serviceRouting.tts` isn't `cloud-proxy`). Read via the **live Capacitor bridge** (`Capacitor.Plugins.Preferences`), because `import("@capacitor/preferences")` can resolve to a web-stub that silently returns nothing (this is why the opt-in didn't arm the first time).

6. **Text brain → Cerebras Gemma** — swapped `gpt-oss-120b` → `gemma-4-31b` (matches the dedicated cloud agent). Verified live.

7. **MP3 playback** — added an `<audio>`-element fallback for `decodeAudioData` failures... which then revealed LightOS has **no MP3 codec at all** (see blocker above). Fallback is in place for WebViews that *do* have MP3 but not this one.

**Regression to note:** the APK rebuilds for the web-bundle fixes were built without the voice-lib staging flags, so the APK **dropped `libelizavoicejni.so`** → the bionic host can't start → **local on-device voice is currently broken on the shipped APK** (cloud voice unaffected). Libs are saved; restore or rebuild with the voice-lib pin to bring local voice back.

---

### 🏗️ Architecture notes (for whoever picks this up)
- **Two separate capture paths.** Composer dictate (Mic icon) → `useVoiceChat.startListening`. Hands-free "talk" (waveform) → `useShellController.startCapture` → `createVoiceCapture`. They do **not** share code — a fix in one doesn't cover the other (this cost several rounds).
- **`useShellVoiceOutput` is output-only** (TTS); it uses `useVoiceChat` but the mic is owned entirely by `startCapture`.
- **Web UI is baked into the APK** (`assets/public`, no `server.url` in `capacitor.config`) → every UI change needs `build:web` + rsync to the platform dir + `gradlew assembleDebug` + reinstall. No hot-swap.
- **Deferred boot is slow on LP3** (~2 min; vision plugin alone ~25 s). The elizacloud *routes* register at the very end of the app-route tail, so `/api/{asr,tts}/cloud` **404 transiently** right after boot — poll `agent.log` for `elizacloud:routes` before testing (not a bug).

### 🎙️ End-of-turn detection + STT (answering "is it the best?")
- **End-of-turn:** works. Two layers — an **energy VAD** (`DEFAULT_LOCAL_ASR_AUTO_STOP`: `silenceMs: 650`, RMS threshold `0.003`) ends a turn after 650 ms of silence, plus a **semantic TurnAggregator** in converse mode so a mid-clause pause doesn't cut off. It's **silence-based**, so long pauses split into multiple turns and there's ~0.65 s of trailing-silence latency.
- **STT model:** **OpenAI Whisper** via Eliza Cloud (`/voice/stt`, provider `openai`/`whisper`). Accurate and robust, but the client path is **batch** (record full utterance → upload whole clip), so **no live word-by-word transcript**.
- **Streaming reality:** text generation **streams** (Cerebras SSE) and pipelines **sentence-by-sentence** into TTS (speech starts before the full reply is done). But **STT is batch** and **TTS returns per-sentence clips** (not byte-streamed). So it is *not* fully token-streamed end-to-end.

### 🚀 What could be better / recommendations
- **Streaming STT** (Deepgram Nova-3 / streaming Whisper) → live transcript + lower latency vs record-then-upload.
- **Neural end-of-turn detection** (LiveKit turn-detector / Krisp) → semantic turn-taking instead of a fixed 650 ms silence window (no pause-splitting, snappier responses).
- **Chunked/streamed TTS audio** → start speaking a sentence before its full clip arrives.
- **WAV output from cloud TTS** → the concrete fix for the MP3-codec-less WebView (see blocker).
- **Codec capability detection** → detect no-MP3 WebViews and auto-request WAV.

### 📋 Remaining work
- [ ] Cloud TTS returns WAV (or client MP3 decoder) → **make voice audible on LP3** (top priority).
- [ ] Restore `libelizavoicejni.so` in the APK build (voice-lib staging) → local on-device voice back.
- [ ] Fix the native local TTS path (`TalkModePlugin.kt` dials dead TCP `127.0.0.1:31337`; should reach the agent's real UDS) → fully-local mic voice.
- [ ] (Optional, larger) streaming STT + neural turn detection for a conversational feel.

*All code changes this session are local commits on a working branch; nothing pushed. Secrets/tokens redacted.*

- Run the required app audit and manually review desktop/mobile loading, success, cancellation, expiry, denial, unavailable, and retry states.11:T1240,## Goal

The chat overlay on iOS and Android should be a **native material surface** — real liquid glass (`UIGlassEffect`) on iOS 26+, the Material dynamic-palette panel on Android 12+ — wrapped via Capacitor, with everything piped between native and web, and web-rendered CSS glass as the fallback tier on web/desktop/older OS versions. Optimized for speed: the native tier replaces the WebView's per-frame `backdrop-filter: blur(30px)` on the dragged sheet (the single biggest GPU/battery cost per #9141) with an OS-composited material.

## What already exists (after the GlassBridge parity PR)

- `GlassBridge` Capacitor plugin on **both** platforms with an identical JS API (`attachGlass` / `updateRect` / `detachGlass` / `setGrouping` / `isAvailable`): iOS 26 `UIGlassEffect` (`packages/app-core/platforms/ios/App/App/GlassBridge.swift`), Android 12+ Material panel (`packages/app-core/platforms/android/.../GlassBridgePlugin.java`).
- The TS tier system: `packages/ui/src/glass/` — `useNativeGlass()` (`native` / `css-refraction` / `css-frosted`), `GlassSurface` (attach-on-mount, ResizeObserver rect sync, transparent element on the native tier), memoized availability probe, CSS fallback identical on every tier.
- The chat sheet's CSS glass (`ContinuousChatOverlay.tsx` — `blur(30px) saturate(1.4)` + rim + sheen on the inset sheet).

## The blocker: the wallpaper is web-rendered

The native material sits **under** the WebView and shows through only where the page is transparent all the way down. Today `AppBackground` (shader/image wallpaper) renders in the DOM — so behind the chat sheet there are always web pixels, and an under-WebView glass region would show the black window background instead of the wallpaper. This is why the sheet still uses the CSS tier.

## Architecture to land

1. **Native-hosted wallpaper (the enabling move).** Extend the bridge (or a sibling `WallpaperBridge`) with `setBackdrop({ imageUrl?, color? })`:
   - iOS: a `UIImageView`/solid layer inserted below the WebView; Android: an `ImageView`/drawable below the WebView.
   - Web: when the native tier is available and the active `BackgroundConfig` is an **image** background, `AppBackground` pipes the image to native (through the existing content-addressed media store URL) and stops painting it in the DOM; shader (animated) backgrounds stay web-rendered and force the CSS tier.
   - Background changes (the `background:apply` view event / BACKGROUND action) re-pipe on change.
2. **Chat sheet adoption.** On the native tier with a native-hosted wallpaper:
   - The inset sheet drops its CSS `backdrop-filter` + fill (keeps rim + sheen overlays, exactly the `GlassSurface` contract) and attaches a `GlassBridge` region at the sheet's rect.
   - **Rest-anchored, CSS during drags:** attach/update on detent settle (spring rest), detach (or freeze) during active drags and fall back to the CSS material for the drag's duration — the bridge rect sync is per-call, not per-frame, and the iOS `updateRect` animates 0.15s. This keeps 60fps drags off the JS→native bridge entirely.
   - Full-bleed stays opaque web paint (nothing to see through; no blur to save).
3. **Pill + menus** adopt `GlassSurface` the same way once the wallpaper is native (they are stable chrome — the primitive's intended anchors).
4. **Perf proof.** Before/after GPU/battery numbers on device for the dragged sheet (the #9141 measurement path), plus frame-time traces during drag on both tiers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `setBackdrop` piped end-to-end on iOS + Android with image backgrounds; shader backgrounds cleanly stay on the CSS tier (no black holes, ever).
- [ ] Chat sheet renders real `UIGlassEffect` on an iOS 26 device/sim and the Material panel on an Android 12+ device/emu, over the piped wallpaper, at every detent; CSS tier during drags with no visible pop at the handoff.
- [ ] Web/desktop/older-OS fall back to the current CSS glass with zero visual change.
- [ ] XCUITest + Android e2e legs assert the tier attribute + screenshot the sheet at rest and mid-drag on both platforms (per-platform capture per CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Frame-time/battery before/after captured and attached.

## Constraints

- No second glass primitive — everything goes through `packages/ui/src/glass/` (`GlassSurface`/`useNativeGlass`).
- One content-addressed media store — the wallpaper pipe reuses `/api/media/<sha256>` URLs, no new file store (#8876).
- Error policy: bridge failures degrade to the CSS tier via the existing `isNativeGlassAvailable` probe (J4) — never a black region.

## Scope

Integrate the **Arsenal Decision Engine** as an external MCP tool provider, enabling ElizaOS DeFi agents (Otaku, plugin-maxia yield scanners) to evaluate Impermanent Loss and compute Breakeven Corridor bounds before allocating capital to constant-product / full-range AMM pools.

The engine is a **stateless risk firewall** — complementary to existing DeFi plugins, not redundant. No existing ElizaOS plugin computes IL boundaries or breakeven corridors.

**Mathematical model (v2.0.0 — live API schema):**

R_net = accumulated_yield_pct − impermanent_loss_pct

- `accumulated_yield_pct = APY × (days_held / 365) × 100`
- `impermanent_loss_pct = |2√(price_ratio) / (1 + price_ratio) − 1| × 100`
- Transaction Gas and Hedging Costs: roadmap v3.0, not in current schema.

Three input parameters: `apy`, `price_ratio`, `days_held`. O(1) algebraic — no LLM, no hallucination, < 15ms.

**Resources:**
- Live MCP gateway: `https://api.arsenal-quant.com/mcp/evaluate`
- Discovery card: `https://api.arsenal-quant.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
- Repository & backtest methodology: [Faouzi122/Arsenal-Quant-Project](https://github.com/Faouzi122/Arsenal-Quant-Project)
- [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) (search: `arsenal-decision-engine`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Agent queries `/mcp/evaluate` during preflight before any pool interaction
- [ ] Plugin handles L402 `402 Payment Required` flow (extract macaroon, pay invoice, retry with proof). PaymentGateway middleware is x402-ready (USDC on Base/Solana) to align with ElizaOS wallet infra
- [ ] Free sandbox tier (3 requests/IP/hour) works without payment setup for development and CI
- [ ] Plugin submitted via `elizaos publish` flow

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)16:T18a2,## Realtime voice: integrated Phase-1 slice (server + client + live-provider evidence)

One vertical slice, per Definition of Done: server, browser client, and the evidence rig that proved them against **live Deepgram Flux + Cartesia Sonic**, in a single reviewable unit. Nothing here is a seam, a stub, or UI ahead of capability.

### What this is
- **Server** (`packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/**`, `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/voice-session/**`): mint route (short-lived scoped JWT, jti, aud-bound), consent-nonce precondition (server-enforced, SEC-21), WS handler with hello-first headerless auth (WebView 113 cannot set WS headers), revoke-to-silence (SEC-6: revocation severs live provider sockets), server-derived usage metering (SEC-15: client never trusted for cost), interruption pipeline under a single voiceTurnId (cancel TTS -> abort SSE -> flush downlink -> `interrupted`), uplink re-framing to Flux's 2560B/80ms frames.
- **Client** (`packages/ui/src/voice/voice-session-*.ts`): mint -> hello-first WSS -> full event handling; mic capture with runtime-verified AudioWorklet + ScriptProcessor fallback (WebView 113); streaming PCM playback (no decodeAudioData full-clip barrier); barge-in flushes local playback before server ack; re-mint on revoked/expired token (no reconnect with a dead token); maps onto the existing unified voice status from #15924 (no second state system).
- **Evidence harness** (`packages/tools/voice-evidence-harness`): one command drives baseline / barge-in / error-auth scenarios and fails loudly if any stage or artifact is missing. `--target=real` boots the REAL server code (real jwt/consent/session/registry/metering/reframer/adapters; only the socket transport is a documented node shim in place of Workers `WebSocketPair`).

### Flag
`VOICE_REALTIME_WS_ENABLED` (default off) is consumed at the WS route: mint returns 503 `voice_realtime_disabled` when off; the evidence run exercises it ON. Real runtime consumer, not a dead flag.

### Live-provider evidence (run against the REAL server, this branch)
Evidence pack (WS transcript with tokens redacted, input/output WAVs, both-side logs, stage timings, domain rows, SHA-256 index, MP4): `evidence/voice-e2e/2026-07-10T15-37-44-748Z-real-server/` (artifacts attached below; full pack retained outside repo, hashes in the index).

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| baseline (real speech in -> transcript -> LLM -> real audio out) | PASS |
| barge-in (interrupt mid-speech) | PASS, **0 post-interrupt downlink frames** |
| error-auth (bad provider key) | PASS, typed `stt_transport_error`, no ready, no audio |

Measured stage deltas (baseline, live providers, monotonic clock; missing stages report `not_reached`, never zero):
- mint -> ready: **10.5ms**
- stt_final -> llm_first_text: 834ms
- llm_first_text -> tts_first_frame: 1273ms
- **stt_final -> tts_first_frame: 2107ms** (see "Latency" below)
- transcript verbatim: "What is the weather like in Denver today?"; 1.8MB real Cartesia audio captured.

### Real bugs found ONLY by the live boot (fixed in this branch, with regression tests)
1. `end_audio` advisory frame was treated as fatal `control_unknown_type` and killed the turn.
2. Empty-transcript finalization sent Cartesia a live 400 ("No valid transcripts passed") -> tts_error, zero audio. Finalization now holds one phrase back so the terminal phrase closes the context with `continue:false`.
3. Harness `stop()` hung on half-open sockets under bun canary drain-exit.
4. Harness error-auth gate accepted only one error shape; the real adapter emits `transport_error`.

### Latency (honest)
2107ms stt_final -> first audio frame is above our 1.2s target. The measured split shows two roughly equal legs (LLM first-token 834ms, TTS first-byte 1273ms). Optimization is scoped as immediate follow-up on this same evidence rig (candidates: eager-EOT speculative LLM start, TTS warm-context reuse, first-phrase fast-path). The rig measures every run, so improvements land with numbers, not adjectives.

### Tests
124 green under bun canary (CI's bun): 31 cloud-api session, 33 cloud-shared voice-session, 60 ui client. Full WS lifecycle, barge-in zero-post-cancel, revoke <=500ms, JWT expiry/revocation/claim-mismatch, metering enforcement, hello-first, malformed/oversized frames, PCM golden vectors, playback ordering, visibility-suspend.

# Risks

**Medium.** This adds an opt-in ambient path to the existing pendant insights route and memory. Risks are model cost accounting, digest idempotence, and derived-memory merge behavior. Ambient defaults off, server caps calls at 48/day, canonical citations are filtered after generation, and current conversation scheduler tests remain green.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Extends the existing pendant insight pipeline, route, schema, prompt, and memory. No second store or scheduler is introduced.
- Adds ambient rolling extraction over only newly finalized canonical segment IDs plus a bounded finalized context tail.
- Handles late finalization across ordinal gaps using persisted processed IDs, so a pending segment is not lost when later finalized.
- Persists empty ambient checkpoints to avoid replaying quiet windows.
- Adds bounded all-day digest chunking and deterministic merge into one owner/agent/session/local-day memory.
- Adds grounded digest summary, nullable-owner action items, commitments, follow-ups, notable moments, people/topics/quotes, and canonical citation filtering.
- Adds server-derived user-local day identity from the trusted runtime `TIMEZONE` setting.
- Adds deterministic normalized-content dedupe with server-recomputed keys and merged citations.
- Enforces min 8 segments, 300-second cadence, and a server-clamped 48-call daily LLM budget before calls begin. Multi-chunk digests reserve every chunk call atomically.
- Adds a synthetic all-day fixture mixing meetings, errands, casual chat, pending hypotheses, and eager rows.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature, opt-in and backward compatible by default.

# Documentation changes needed?

The route contracts and lifecycle/cost invariants are documented inline. No user-facing documentation surface exists yet for ambient mode.

Part of #13432 — the **cloud route path** slice (claim: "Lane: [fable-hard-lane]", 2026-07-09): quota/cost preflight, conservative max-upload enforcement, resumable chunk-upload routes + progress state, retention, and batch delete — wired to the already-landed `@elizaos/import-conversations` core primitives (preflight #13901, resumable state #14266, artifact policy #14256). The core package is not modified.

## What this adds

**Routes** (`packages/cloud/api`, all org-scoped via `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg`):

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/imports/preflight` | Size + tenant-quota admission **before any bytes**; typed fail-fast DTOs |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads` | Init resumable session (preflight → atomic quota reservation → batch row → R2 multipart → core session state) |
| `PUT /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId/chunks/:chunkIndex` | Digest-verified chunk append (offset/length/sha256 validated by the core primitive); idempotent duplicate retry; typed conflict |
| `GET /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId` | Progress + exact missing byte ranges (resume support) |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId/complete` | Whole-or-nothing: missing chunks ⇒ typed `upload_interrupted` with missing ranges — **never a silent partial import**; idempotent retry |
| `DELETE /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId` | Abort: R2 multipart abort + quota release, idempotent |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads/direct` | Small exports within the conservative direct ceiling; `resumable_required` above it |
| `GET /api/v1/imports/batches`, `GET/DELETE /api/v1/imports/batches/:batchId` | Batch inspection + retention-policy batch delete with per-artifact accounting |
| `GET /api/cron/cleanup-expired-import-uploads` | Retention sweep (registered in the `0 */6 * * *` cron fanout) |

**Use-case layer** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/conversation-imports.ts`): all business logic lives here; routes only validate shape and return DTOs (`importFailureHttpStatus` maps stable codes → status). Storage quota rides the existing `org_storage_quota` atomic reserve/release; reservation is transferred to the raw artifact at complete, released exactly once on abort/expiry/delete.

**Persistence**: new `import_batches` / `import_upload_sessions` / `import_artifacts` tables (migration `0175_conversation_imports.sql`), org-scoped repositories, optimistic-concurrency chunk state writes reconciled via the core `mergeResumableUploadSessions` primitive.

**Storage**: `RuntimeR2Bucket` widened additively with the optional R2 multipart surface (fail-fast 503 when the binding lacks it — never buffer 1 GiB in Worker memory). Object keys follow the core artifact layout `conversation-imports/<tenant>/apps/<app>/batches/<batch>/<kind>/<sha256>.<ext>`.

**Config** (all optional, malformed values fail closed): `IMPORT_MAX_DIRECT_UPLOAD_BYTES`, `IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (defaults = core `DEFAULT_IMPORT_LIMITS`: 25 MiB / 1 GiB), `IMPORT_RAW_RETENTION_MS` (default = core 7-day), `IMPORT_MAX_EMBEDDING_UNITS`, `IMPORT_MAX_CONVERSATIONS` (per-import cost ceilings).

## Contract items covered (from #12071 / #13432)

- ✅ Object-store raw uploads with **short retention by default** (7-day `expires_at` marker + cron sweep; longer retention requires an explicit reason)
- ✅ **Content-addressed derived artifacts** tied to tenant/app/batch lifecycle (`storeDerivedArtifact`, dedupes identical content)
- ✅ **Tenant quota enforcement before import** (preflight + atomic reservation before any bytes)
- ✅ **Fail-fast typed errors** for quota/cost overrun (`quota_storage_exceeded`, `quota_embedding_exceeded`, `quota_conversations_exceeded`, `upload_too_large`, `resumable_required`)
- ✅ **Conservative configurable max upload size** by default
- ✅ **100MB–1GB imports require resumable chunks + preflight quota** (`requiresResumable`, direct path refuses with `resumable_required`)
- ✅ **Never silently truncate**: complete with missing chunks returns `upload_interrupted` + exact missing ranges; conflicting chunk retries are typed conflicts
- ✅ Batch delete/manage per retention policy with per-artifact success/failure accounting (retryable failures keep the batch alive)
- ✅ Failure DTOs for quota exceeded / upload interrupted / **parser failure** / **partial import** (`parser_failed`, `partial_import` are defined in the shared DTO union with required fields, ready for the executor — see seams)

## Remaining seams (explicitly out of this slice)

- **Import execution** (parse → redact → render → DocumentService → embeddings) consuming completed raw uploads: the step that will *surface* `parser_failed` / `partial_import` and charge **actual** embedding usage against tenant quota (this slice provides the per-import embedding/conversation cost ceilings + the post-parse gate hook via core `estimateBundleUsage`).
- **#13431 UI integration** (tracked separately; UI rows below are N/A).
- **Batch-delete planner core module**: claimed on the issue 2026-07-05 but never landed on `develop`; this slice implements delete accounting in the cloud service against the same semantics (idempotent, per-document accounting, retryable failures) without touching core. If that core module lands, the service loop can delegate to it.
- **Whole-file digest for resumable uploads** is client-declared at init (every chunk is server-side digest-verified by the core primitive; core's `buildImportArtifactDescriptor` hashes bytes itself, which a 1 GiB stream can't provide up front). `buildRawUploadStorageKey` mirrors the core key layout exactly and collapses into a core descriptor-from-digest variant if one is exported later. Direct uploads use the core descriptor with real bytes.
- `@elizaos/import-conversations` is wired via the established source-alias mechanism (tsconfig `paths` + `wrangler.toml [alias]`, same as `@elizaos/core`/`@elizaos/shared` deep aliases) rather than a `package.json` dependency edge — only the three pure core modules (`node:crypto` only) are aliased into the Worker bundle; parsers (node:fs) stay off it. No lockfile change.

1d:T3071,## What

The context-retrieval pass + corpus-wide pseudonym consistency stage of the corpus PII scrub pipeline (stage position: between candidate-mining and the LLM-pass), built entirely on the landed rails — `PiiScrubService` (#14808 slice 1, PR #15139) and the `PII_SCRUB` model seam (#14809, PR #14980) — with **zero changes to either**. No new scheduler, no new queue, no second knowledge-graph store.

Closes #14805

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-pseudonym-map.ts` — one person = one replacement everywhere
- `CorpusPseudonymMap`: cluster-keyed (`entity:<entityId>` from the EntityStore alias backbone — **never surface strings**), extending the session pseudonymizer's deterministic minting (`mintSurrogate`, now exported) from per-session to corpus-persistent: mint seed is `(salt, kind, clusterId, attempt)`, salt persisted inside the (secret) snapshot, so the same person deterministically keeps the same pseudonym across runs, artifact types, and assignment orders.
- **Collision behavior:** two distinct people sharing a name are two clusters with two pseudonyms; an alias claimed by 2+ clusters is **ambiguous** — never blind-substituted (a longest-first self-mapping shields it from partial rewrites by contained shorter aliases), surfaced for model escalation with ALL candidate assignments. A newly learned real alias equal to an existing pseudonym re-mints that cluster with a `supersededPseudonyms` audit trail. Re-homing a platform identity to a second cluster **throws** — identity merges stay in the merge engine.
- **Idempotent upsert** (no duplicate clusters/aliases/identities on re-assign) and **pseudonym stability across ruleset bumps** — a `v<ruleset>` bump re-scrubs content (content-hash markers re-key) with the SAME pseudonyms, so a re-scrub never re-links identities.

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-pseudonym-map-store.ts` — the map is a secret artifact
- The alias→pseudonym map inverts the scrub, so it lives **outside the retrievable corpus**: one dedicated runtime-cache key (`pii:pseudonym-map:v1`, next to the scrub done-markers), never a document/memory row, no ingestion path — unreachable via `searchDocuments` / `searchMessages` / `searchMemories` / `SEARCH_KNOWLEDGE`, never chunked or embedded. Confidentiality is structural, plus at-rest AES-256-GCM (v2 settings-secret scheme, dedicated AAD `elizaos:pii-pseudonym-map:v1` for domain separation, `SECRET_SALT` lifecycle).
- **Fail-closed everywhere:** refuses to persist plaintext; wrong key, tampered ciphertext, non-ciphertext value, or a structurally invalid snapshot all **throw** (deliberately stricter than `decryptStringValue`'s return-original-on-error) — a partial map would silently re-mint pseudonyms for already-mapped people, which is worse than stopping the pipeline.

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-context-pack.ts` — the context-retrieval pass
- `assembleContextPack`: per chunk, resolves candidates through a **structural `EntityStore.resolve` seam** (`PiiEntityResolverStore` matches `packages/agent/src/services/knowledge-graph/entity-store.ts` field-for-field; `entityResolverFromStore(kg.getEntityStore())` wires it with zero adaptation — core does not import agent), gathers related fragments (`DocumentService.searchDocuments`, `runtime.searchMemories` under the embeddings throw-never-fabricate doctrine, `adapter.searchMessages` with explicit roomIds), clusters confident resolutions into the map, and emits the bounded pack + the per-chunk `{entityClusterId, surrogate, kind}` assignment slice — **never the whole map, never a real alias**.
- Failure doctrine: absent sources are structurally skipped and audited in `sourcesQueried`; a wired source that throws **propagates** (rails retry the item) — degraded context silently producing a wrong verdict is the failure mode this pass exists to prevent.
- `buildScrubRequestDraft` folds a chunk + pack into the landed `PII_SCRUB_REQUESTED` payload — the exported interface siblings (#14806 transcript anchors, #14807 audio redaction span labels) consume for corpus-consistent replacements.
- `pii-pseudonymizer.ts`: additive `export` on `mintSurrogate` + `compileReplacer` only; no behavior change (fuzz + unit suites green).

1f:T3bae,Part of #14807 — the audio-redaction core: span production, duration-preserving mute/bleep execution, content-addressed redacted-variant storage, and the separable re-transcribe-verify contract. Residuals (sibling-owned or follow-on wiring) are listed explicitly at the bottom.

## What this adds

**Span production — `@elizaos/shared/audio-redaction` (pure, browser+node safe)**
- `matchPiiSpansToWords`: text-PII verdicts (the `span` strings from tier-0 detectors / `PII_SCRUB` verdicts, with optional pseudonym labels from #14805 accepted as plain input) are located inside **raw timed-ASR word spans** (`TranscriptWord` — no dependency on #14806's unlanded anchor seam). Matching is separator-insensitive in both directions: `"John Smith"` across two ASR words and `"555 0123"` inside one fused ASR word `"5550123."` both match; **every** occurrence is windowed. Unlocatable PII returns in `unmatched` — the caller must fail typed (fail-closed, per @LauraGPT's acceptance note); it is never silently empty.
- `mergeRedactionSpans`: pad → clamp to `[0, duration]` → merge overlaps/adjacency/containment into non-overlapping integer-ms windows; malformed spans **throw** rather than drop. Default pad is **250 ms, empirically calibrated** (see evidence: at 150 ms a boundary digit fragment of the planted phone number survived; at 250–300 ms nothing PII-shaped survives re-transcription).

**Execution — `packages/agent/src/api/audio-redaction.ts`**
- **Pure-TS PCM16 WAV lane** (every runtime, no ffmpeg): sample zeroing (mute) / phase-anchored 1 kHz sine (bleep). Byte geometry untouched, so duration is preserved **exactly** and output is **bit-deterministic**. This covers the voice pipeline's native 16 kHz PCM16 WAV with zero dependencies — the constrained-runtime criterion.
- **ffmpeg lane** (desktop/server only) for ogg/opus, m4a/aac, mp3, webm using the issue's empirically verified graphs — `volume=0:enable='between(t,S,E)+…'` (mute), `sine=f=1000` + gated `amix=duration=first:normalize=0` (bleep) — with `-bitexact` for deterministic bytes. Per-container duration assertions: wav+ogg exact (±2 ms probe slack), aac/mp3 ±(1024/sampleRate)s (one encoder frame); drift beyond tolerance throws `AUDIO_REDACTION_DURATION_DRIFT`. A lossy container on a host with **no ffmpeg** (mobile/workers) throws typed `AUDIO_REDACTION_UNSUPPORTED` — observable, never a silent skip.

**Storage — `packages/agent/src/api/audio-redaction-store.ts` (#8876-clean)**
- The redacted variant is **a second object in the ONE content-addressed media store** (`persistMediaBytes` → `${STATE_DIR}/media/<sha256'>.<ext>` served at `/api/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`). No new store, no files table, no `fileId`, no refcount engine. Job key `pii-audio:<originalSha>:v<ruleset>:<mode>:<spanHash>` (the audio analog of the #14808 `pii:<sha>:v<ruleset>` marker). A small capped memo (`audio-redactions.json`, the `background-pins.json` precedent) makes re-runs cheap lookups — it is a cache, not truth: wiping it recomputes to the **identical output sha** (tested). `media-store.ts` gains two additive exports (`storedMediaFileExists`, `mimeForStoredMediaFile`); nothing else in the store changes.

**Verify — `@elizaos/shared/audio-redaction-verify` + agent adapters, deliberately SEPARABLE from the span producer** (per the acceptance note):
- `RedactionTranscriber` contract: audio bytes + language hint in, normalized transcript out, **no timestamps required**. Judgment = PII absence by normalized fuzzy containment (never transcript equality — whisper hallucinates filler over silence) + sentinel presence (over-mute guard). **Zero configured verifiers throws typed** — never a vacuous pass; a backend throw propagates.
- Adapters: `runtimeTranscriptionTranscriber` (registered `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION`, interim purpose), `openAiCompatSttTranscriber` (any self-hosted `/v1/audio/transcriptions` — faster-whisper/FunASR/SenseVoice, the independent-verifier lane), and `energyFixtureTranscriber` (deterministic, model-free RMS + 1 kHz Goertzel over the real bytes, for no-ASR environments; honestly a fixture — it needs the expected word list).

## Problem

The existing `verify` stage performed no verification: it cloned each message and advanced `scrubState` to `verified`. Worse, `corpus scrub --stage verify --target <raw shards>` could read raw input directly and bless it one row at a time, without checking sibling shards, original-value provenance, deletion approval, canaries, attachment bytes, placeholders, or gitleaks.

## Change

- disables the row-level no-op; `corpus:scrub --stage all` now stops at `rewritten`, and direct `--stage verify` fails with a pointer to the corpus-wide command
- adds `corpus:verify`, a non-mutating, fail-closed `jsonl-text-v1` verifier
- snapshots the exact shard set, rejects concurrent shard/artifact changes and unknown JSON fields, and scans the same bytes with structured detectors and gitleaks
- requires an exact manifest plus unambiguous hash-chained ledger, recomputed complete mine candidates, original gazetteer, canary attestation, semantically validated deletion rules/review/approval artifacts, and placeholder registry
- scans every string-bearing message field with core structured PII detectors, regex entities, original-value gazetteer/LHS matching, and production redact patterns
- rejects embedded attachment bytes and malformed, legacy, forged, unregistered, or unused placeholders
- runs gitleaks over each exact shard with the repository config, a timeout, full redaction, mode-0600 transient reports, and fatal cleanup semantics
- emits a canonical self-hashed report containing hashes and structural locations only; no matched text, snippets, raw gitleaks secrets, or gazetteer values
- exports `assertFreshGreenVerification()` so #14773 reruns the complete gate and requires a byte-identical green report immediately before publishing; the self-hash is corruption detection, not authorization

This PR deliberately cannot certify the real corpus yet. #14769 must produce the required deletion approval/attachment disposition, production canary and placeholder-registry artifacts must exist, multimodal/audio verification remains outside the declared scope, and the owner must bind the ≥200-message review to the exact machine report hash.

## Problem

`#15929` serialized only the migration-target lookup+insert: the advisory lock was released when `createTierUpgradeTarget` committed, while managed credential minting, environment writes, the worker-health rollback delete, and `enqueueAgentProvisionOnce` stayed route-level work. A losing concurrent request polled 10s for a job, then independently minted credentials and overwrote the target's environment; the fresh-target compensation wrapper could delete a target already owned by a committed provision job; the target insert hand-assembled `agentSandboxes` values instead of using the canonical builder.

## Fix (retains the #16042 shape the review asked to keep, plus its two blockers)

**One durable single-flight boundary** — `createTierUpgradeTargetWithProvision` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target.ts`):

- **Phase 1 (locked tx):** reattach fast-path + pre-mint quota refusal.
- **Phase 2 (unlocked):** managed environment prepared against a pre-generated target id (the api-key mint runs on its own connection; a candidate key is bound to its caller's own prospective id, never the winner's target).
- **Phase 3 (locked tx, the boundary):** re-check → org-serialized quota assert → target insert through the canonical `buildAgentSandboxInsertValues` builder with the fully-prepared, storage-encrypted environment → **provision job insert in the same transaction** (`provisioningJobService.enqueueAgentProvisionOnceInTx`). Target + job are atomic; the compensation delete is gone; the 10s job poll is gone; worker health is checked before anything durable is minted.

**Blocker 1 — org quota serialization (closing review §1):** both phases acquire the **org-wide `elizaAgentCreateAdvisoryLockSql` BEFORE the per-source tier-upgrade lock** (global order: org → tier-upgrade → provision, documented in `eliza-provision-lock.ts`), so the count→insert window is atomic against ordinary `createAgent`, coding-container creates, and upgrades of a **different** source agent. Regressions: two different-source upgrades racing the last slot, and an upgrade racing `createAgent` at cap-1 — exactly one succeeds in each, proven on PGlite **and on real multi-connection Postgres 16**.

**Blocker 2 — ambiguous-commit credential ownership (closing review §2):** a boundary-transaction rejection is no longer treated as proof of rollback. `resolveOutcomeAfterBoundaryRejection` re-reads durable state on a fresh connection and only then acts:
- candidate id IS the live target → the commit landed; the **committed target+job are recovered and returned**, credential untouched;
- a competitor's target is live → candidate provably unreferenced → revoked, reattach;
- provably absent → revoked, original error stands;
- **verification itself fails → the credential is PRESERVED** (a stranded key is recoverable hygiene debt, #16071; a revoked live-target key breaks the agent) and the uncertainty is logged with both errors.

Typed errors: `ElizaError` codes `TIER_UPGRADE_TARGET_INSERT_FAILED` and `PROVISION_ENQUEUE_AGENT_NOT_FOUND` (message preserved for the routes that map "Agent not found" to 404). Known residual (crash between phase 2 and 3 strands a candidate api-key row with no GC path — pre-existing on the old compensation path too): tracked in #16071.

**Test infrastructure shipped with this** (the coverage lane co-runs every changed suite in ONE bun process, which surfaced two real hazards): module-scope `mock.module` calls execute at preload and clobber the shared `db/helpers`→`db/client` re-export binding under every other suite — all touched suites now install mocks in `beforeAll` and restore from value snapshots in `afterAll`; and drizzle-kit `pushSchema` answers internal errors with a silent `process.exit(1)` — the tier-upgrade suites apply plain DDL (`__tests__/tier-upgrade-pglite-schema.ts`, the `jobs-recovery.test.ts` pattern). Pre-existing eliza-sandbox/provisioning-jobs suites gained genuine cases (builder parity, quota boundary, dispatch payload contract, sweep completeness, failed-turn reservation release, bootstrap window for migration targets, profile/env update semantics), which also carries every changed source file past the tightened per-file LCOV floor (#16038).

## Proof against real multi-connection Postgres (closing review §3)

Disposable `postgres:16` container (`docker run -d -p 5544:5432 …`), fresh databases per run — **not** PGlite:

- **Full single-flight suite (14 tests) on Postgres 16**: the 6-way concurrent burst, the 10.5s delayed winner, both cap-1 quota races, commit-ack-loss recovery and verification-failure preservation all run as genuinely parallel transactions on separate pooled connections with real `pg_advisory_xact_lock` contention → 14 pass / 0 fail. Artifact: [15943-v2-pg-service-suite.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence/15943-v2-pg-service-suite.log)
- **Five concurrent HTTP POSTs through the real route** (real service, repositories, credential mint, job enqueue; auth is the only mocked seam) → all 202, exactly one `created:true`, all five converge on one target id + one job id; row dump shows 1 target / 1 `agent_provision` job / 1 `agent-sandbox:<target>` key. Artifact: [15943-v2-pg-route-5x-concurrent.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence/15943-v2-pg-route-5x-concurrent.log)
- **Failure injection at the commit and enqueue boundaries** runs in the same suite on both engines: enqueue-throw → full rollback (no target/job/key residue) + retry converges; commit-ack-loss → durable pair recovered with live credential; verification-failure → credential preserved, uncertainty surfaced.

**Staging E2E (honest status):** the real-Postgres multi-session proof above is attached; a deployed staging run of five concurrent HTTP requests through the hosted API + provisioning worker needs a credentialed staging deploy this lane does not have. Offered as an immediate follow-up if access is granted.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)22:T2fe7,## What & why

Closes #15796 — a newly spun-up agent (cloud container, fresh desktop install, new user) had no guided path to GitHub credentials, so every GitHub-touching capability (`TASKS_MANAGE_ISSUES`, `TASKS_SUBMIT_WORKSPACE`, repo provisioning) failed until the operator discovered the right setting by reading source.

This makes GitHub credentials a **first-class guided setup step**, reusing the #15749 device-flow primitive as promised in the claim: the Settings → Coding Agents **GitHub connection card** now offers *Sign in with GitHub* (OAuth device flow) alongside the existing PAT paste, stores the obtained token **per-agent via runtime settings + the existing credential store (not process env)**, and mid-task credential failures now point at the setup step.

**Complementary PR:** #15844 (same issue, docs slice for `plugin-agent-orchestrator` README) is open from a parallel lane — zero file overlap with this PR (this PR touches `workspace-github.ts` source + `packages/docs/connectors/github.md`; that one touches the orchestrator README/CLAUDE/AGENTS).

**Out of scope (owner decision pending, per the claim):** the cloud per-agent identity policy — bot account vs user PAT vs GitHub App installation for cloud-provisioned agents. Noted as an open question in the docs; not decided here.

**`elizaos` CLI:** intentionally **not** added. Per `packages/elizaos/CLAUDE.md` the CLI is a standalone, dependency-light scaffolding tool that does not import the runtime; the device flow needs the running agent's HTTP surface and per-agent settings, so a CLI login step would bloat it with runtime/server concerns for no benefit. The dashboard card is the guided surface.

## Changes

**`@elizaos/plugin-github`**
- New `src/device-flow.ts` — TypeScript port of the #15749 primitive (`scripts/lifeops/github-device-login.mjs`): `device_code` never leaves the server, server-owned polling interval (honors `slow_down`, throttles eager clients locally), 409 owner-setup vs 502 upstream error taxonomy, expiry sweep — plus one addition: **flows are bound to the agent that started them** (`agentKey`), so on a multi-agent host one agent's runtime can never poll another agent's flow.
- Two new routes: `POST /api/github/device/start` (409 with an actionable owner-setup message when `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` is absent) and `POST /api/github/device/poll` (`pending`/`denied`/`expired`, or on grant: validate against GitHub `/user` → persist via the existing `github-credentials` store → apply to the live runtime per-agent via `setSetting("GITHUB_TOKEN", …, true)`). No second storage mechanism; no process-env write (env leaks to every agent on a multi-tenant host — the existing boot-time `applySavedTokenToEnv` behavior for `gh`/`git` subprocess inheritance is unchanged).
- `GET /api/github/token` now reports `deviceFlowAvailable`; the PAT `POST` also applies the live runtime setting (connect → retry works without a restart); `DELETE` disconnects the live runtime too.
- **Latent bug fixed:** `readJsonBody` now prefers the canonical dispatcher's pre-parsed `req.body` — an `application/json` POST (the exact shape the dashboard card sends) previously read an already-consumed stream and returned 400 through `tryHandleRuntimePluginRoute` (the existing e2e dodged it by posting `text/plain`, with a comment acknowledging the behavior). Covered by a new test that posts real `application/json` through the real dispatcher.
- `action-helpers.needsClientError` now points at the setup card, not just env var names.

**`@elizaos/plugin-task-coordinator`**
- `GitHubConnectionCard` grows the guided path: *Sign in with GitHub* → prominent short code + `github.com/login/device` link (opened externally) → poll at the server-provided cadence → connected; denied/expired resolve to actionable errors with the PAT fallback suggested; Cancel really stops the poll loop (generation-guarded timers, cleaned on unmount). Orange accent only, no blue, accent → darker-accent hover (kit `Button` variants).
- New real-browser screenshot harness `src/__e2e__/{github-card-fixture.tsx, build-github-card-fixture.mjs, run-github-card-shot.mjs}` (modeled on the existing `run-dashboard-shot.mjs`; build under bun, drive under node).

**`@elizaos/plugin-agent-orchestrator`**
- `workspace-github.ts` missing-credential errors now point at Settings → Coding Agents (the mid-task failure → setup-step UX from the issue).

**Docs**
- `packages/docs/connectors/github.md`: new *Guided credential setup (dashboard)* section — PAT vs device sign-in comparison, **vault/settings vs env** (multi-tenant leak warning), and the open cloud identity-policy note.
- plugin-github + plugin-task-coordinator `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (kept identical) + plugin-github README updated for the new routes/card.

24:T324b,Implements #15355 — the first-class shared→dedicated agent upgrade, per the cloud-hardening scoping comment on the issue (2026-07-09T01:44Z).

## What ships

**1. Backend — `POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:agentId/upgrade-tier`** (new route; distinct from the `agent_upgrade`/`downgrade` image blue/green machinery)
- **Ownership + tier validation:** org-scoped read (cross-org indistinguishable from missing → 404, no oracle); only `execution_tier === 'shared'` upgrades (409 `not_shared_tier`); only a `running` source (409 `agent_not_running`).
- **Hosting-runway credit gate:** `checkAgentTierUpgradeCreditGate` requires balance above `AGENT_PRICING.UPGRADE_MINIMUM_BALANCE` ($0.72 = 3 days × `DAILY_RUNNING_COST` $0.24) — stricter than the $0.10 create minimum, because a dedicated agent burns credits continuously. Denials reuse the canonical `insufficientCredits402` body, now carrying the **enforced** threshold in `requiredBalance` (and the warn log reports the real threshold too).
- **Server-side identity copy:** `agent_name` / `character_id` / `agent_config` / `environment_vars` are read from the shared row on the server (the compat create route never reads the source row and clients can't reconstruct identity from DTOs). Platform-reserved env keys (`ELIZA_API_TOKEN`, `ELIZA_CLOUD_AGENT_ID`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, …) are stripped so the target mints its own identity; user BYO env — including `enc:v1:` ciphertext — survives verbatim (same-org envelope key; the storage encryptor never double-encrypts).
- **Provisioning:** dedicated-always create under the balance-tiered org quota (`forceCreate` semantics; 429 on quota), managed env preparation, worker-health check at the enqueue boundary with explicit row rollback, real `agent_provision` job + 202 with the standard `polling` envelope. Create→enqueue failures roll the fresh row back (orphan-cleanup wrapper).
- **Retry idempotency, tier-checked:** the target records `__agentUpgradedFrom: <sharedId>` in the reserved `__agent` config namespace (client input can never forge it at create time — new `AGENT_UPGRADED_FROM_KEY` in `eliza-agent-config.ts`). A retried POST **reattaches** to the live in-flight target (2xx `alreadyInProgress: true`, same `dedicatedAgentId`, active job reused) instead of minting a second container. Reattach requires the candidate to be `execution_tier === 'dedicated-always'` — `agent_config` is PATCHable, so a marker planted on a non-dedicated row is never treated as a live target (covered by a route test that fails without the check).

**2. Client — chat continuity via the existing #15313 handoff stack**
- New `packages/ui/src/cloud/handoff/start-tier-upgrade.ts`: `runSharedToDedicatedUpgradeHandoff()` wraps `startCloudAgentHandoff` (readiness poll → idempotent transcript import; canonical conversation id === shared agent id) and deletes the shared bridge **only** on a confirmed `switched`/`switched-empty` — awaited and reported (`sharedBridgeDeleted`), never fire-and-forget. On `timed-out`/`failed` the user keeps the working shared agent and a retry resumes the same upgrade.

**3. UI — "Upgrade to Dedicated" on the agent detail page** (next to the #15639 deactivate flow, `packages/ui/src/cloud/instances/components/agent-actions.tsx`)
- Shared-tier-only action; confirm dialog spells out the continuous burn ($0.24/day, $0.01/hr) and the $0.72 / 3-days-of-hosting minimum **before** anything changes — figures from the same `AGENT_PRICING` constants the gate enforces (client only displays; a 402's message renders the server's numbers verbatim).
- Confirm fires the real POST; progress rides a reload-free `useJobPoller` instance (the default hard reload would kill the in-page transcript move) + a whole-span progress line; on a confirmed switch the page navigates to the dedicated agent; a failed shared-bridge delete is surfaced, not hidden. i18n catalog entries added (`en.json`).

## Design notes

- **Naming trap respected:** the existing `agent_upgrade` job / `downgrade` route are image blue/green — this route is `upgrade-tier` and mints a new record, per the issue scoping.
- **Reattach over dedupe-by-lock:** the marker scan is best-effort dedup for real retry shapes (double-click, reload, second tab); a sub-second concurrent race is bounded by the per-org agent quota enforced under the create's advisory lock. Only a `dedicated-always` row can be reattached to — the marker alone is not proof of a migration target.
- **Reattach skips the credit gate** deliberately: nothing new is minted, and gating it would strand a user whose balance dipped after the (gated) mint while the container is already billing — ongoing solvency belongs to the billing cron + low-credit shutdown.
- **Warm pool skipped** on the upgrade path: upgrades are not latency-critical and always take the async job path (comment in route).
- Downgrade story stays suspend / deactivate / delete (shown in the confirm copy); true tier-downgrade (reverse transcript export) does not exist today and is out of scope per the issue scoping.

Closes #15355.

25:T3d1e,Part of #14808 — the **CLOUD-lane rails slice** (slice 3 of the sequence in [sol-orch]'s design note; slice 1 LOCAL lane landed in #15139, the #14809 seam landed in #14980). The issue **stays open** for the remaining slices — see "Acceptance coverage" below for exactly what this PR does and does not close.

## What this adds

Runs corpus PII scrub batches on Eliza Cloud using **only existing rails** — the generic `jobs` table + `jobsRepository` claim/retry machinery and the CF cron fan-out. **No new scheduler, no new queue.**

| Piece | Where | Precedent mirrored |
|---|---|---|
| `pii_scrub` job type + `enqueuePiiScrubBatch` (202 front door) + budget-bounded drain `processPendingPiiScrubJobs` | `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/pii-scrub-jobs.ts` | `provisioning-jobs.ts` cycle (claim `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` → execute → `incrementAttempt` backoff → `recoverStaleJobs` backstop); R2 offload for large payloads comes free via `prepareJobInsertData` |
| Tenant-scoped content-hash done-markers | `pii_scrub_markers` table + repository (`tryCreate` = `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) | `webhook_events.tryCreate` two-tier dedupe; key shape **identical** to the LOCAL lane (`pii:<sha256(content)>:v<rulesetVersion>`, `packages/core/src/security/pii-scrub-markers.ts`) so work never duplicates across lanes |
| Per-item executor seam (tier-0 floor + injected escalation) | `pii-scrub-executor.ts` | Reuses the merged #14809 seam primitives (`detectPii`, `assertValidScrubResult`, `PiiScrubFabricationError`) — throw-never-fabricate is inherited, not re-implemented |
| Org-scoped enqueue + progress routes | `POST/GET /api/v1/pii-scrub/jobs[/:id]` | `v1/files` route conventions (`requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg`, zod, DTO built in the use-case layer) |
| Cron drain consumer | `POST /api/cron/process-pii-scrub-jobs` + `CRON_FANOUT` `*/5` entry | `process-stripe-queue` / `reconcile-video-generations` Worker-cron consumers |

### Design decisions a reviewer should check

- **`pii_scrub` is deliberately NOT added to `JOB_TYPES`** (`provisioning-job-types.ts`): the provisioning daemon claims `Object.values(JOB_TYPES)` and its `executeJob` throws "Unknown job type" for rows it can't run — which would burn their retry budget into permanent failed-row noise (the exact failure-flooding class #15737 documents). The generic `jobsRepository` supports independent job types by design; `pii_scrub` gets its own cron consumer instead.
- **Retry classification** (#15737 lesson): structurally-invalid payloads (including a payload org that disagrees with the row's authenticated org) fail **permanently on first sight, zero attempts burned**; a drain-budget stop requeues via `retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts` (finished items are already marker-protected); only real failures consume the bounded budget and then fail loudly.
- **Fail-closed on the rails**: an item whose candidate spans exceed the tier-0 floor with no escalation handler registered throws (`PiiScrubFabricationError`) → no done-marker, bounded retries, loud failed job. Un-inspected content is never passed as clean.
- **Tenant isolation**: markers are unique per `(organization_id, marker_key)` — one org's scrub can never mark (or probe) another org's content; jobs read cross-org as 404.
- **Worker stub**: `detectPii`/`assertValidScrubResult`/`PiiScrubFabricationError` are re-exported from the REAL core modules in `stubs/elizaos-core.ts` (pure, Worker-safe leaves) — same pattern the stub already uses for `security/redact`.
- Executor payload/stage interface stays **generic** (itemRef + content + candidateSpans + contextPack): the scrub content stages (#14805/#14806/#14807, in flight by siblings) and the server compute lanes plug in without touching these rails.

## Acceptance coverage (issue #14808)

Covered by this slice, all under real PGlite `bun:test`:
- ✅ **Cloud enqueue → claim → execute → complete** on `jobsRepository` rails, progress advancing queued→running→done with item counts on the job row.
- ✅ **Crash-resume**: worker killed mid-batch (claimed row + 2/4 durable markers, no cursor anywhere) → stale sweep re-arms → re-claim executes **only** the unmarked items; zero duplicate markers (asserted via a grouped marker-table dump).
- ✅ **Queue-consumer retry semantics**: bounded attempts + backoff, permanent-vs-transient classification, budget requeue without attempt burn, completed rows never re-swept.
- ✅ **Exactly-once**: two workers claiming concurrently → one wins (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`); two workers finishing the same item → exactly one marker row.
- ✅ **Tenant isolation** incl. cross-tenant probes and the payload-org/row-org tripwire.
- ✅ **Throw-never-fabricate** exercised on the rails (residue + no handler → quarantined item, failed job, no marker) and at the executor (fabricated verdicts, stale-ruleset verdicts, dropped candidates all rejected by the seam's own validator).

NOT covered here (remaining #14808 slices, issue stays open):
- ❌ Server compute lanes: Cerebras passthrough registration + billing-ledger row, and/or vllm container path — the `PiiScrubEscalationHandler` seam is their plug point.
- ❌ `cloud:mock` full-stack e2e + **one LIVE Cerebras bulk run with usage/billing evidence** (requires the compute lane above).
- ❌ `routing/features.ts` `PII_SCRUB` feature id + cloud-proxy request path (agent-originated cloud scrub), the non-blocking latency harness, and the LOCAL `*.real.test.ts` model lane (LOCAL slice 2).
- ❌ The both-lanes hard gate — closes on #14808 itself once all slices land.

26:Ta3c,## What
Two additions that let a user talk to the agent from a Discord **group DM** — a context where a bot can never read the message stream, only receive interactions:

1. **`/ask <message>`** — routes free text through the real message service and returns the agent's reply as the interaction response (chunked across `editReply` + `followUp` for >2000 chars). Works everywhere (servers, bot DMs, group DMs); degrades cleanly when the runtime/message service isn't ready or the message is empty.
2. **Opt-in group-DM / user-install commands** — `transformCommandToDiscordApi` sets `contexts: [guild, bot-DM, private-channel]` + `integrationTypes: [guild, user]` on non-guild-only commands when `DISCORD_USER_INSTALL` is enabled. Guild-only commands stay pinned to the guild context; an explicit `contexts` array still wins.

## Why off by default
Discord **rejects** user-install command registration unless the application is configured as user-installable in the developer portal. So `DISCORD_USER_INSTALL` defaults to `false` (current behavior: guild + bot-DM), and operators opt in after enabling User Install in the portal.

## Tests (10; full plugin suite 315/315)
- Transform opt-in matrix: default omits contexts; `userInstall` adds `[0,1,2]` + `[0,1]`; guild-only stays `[0]`; explicit `contexts` respected.
- `/ask` handler: routes text into the message service, DM channel-type off-guild, empty-message reject (no runtime touch), no-service graceful degrade, long-answer chunking across editReply + followUps.

## Files (all new, all under `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/**` + one config regex extension)

- `helpers/pwa-context.ts` — installed-PWA / iOS-lifecycle emulation seam (standalone display-mode, `visibilitychange`/`pagehide`/`freeze`/`resume` in iOS order, `devicechange` route-swap, an AudioContext registry that models a real suspend→resume transition, not a permanent mask).
- `helpers/voice-latency-artifact.ts` — consumer-only harvester for the `voice.*` performance marks (emitted by #15931) + AudioContext probe; writes one JSON artifact per test to `test-results/.voice/` and attaches it.
- `voice-pwa-lifecycle.spec.ts` — installed-PWA gesture→permission→capture, suspended-context resume, background/foreground (fresh-gesture-required), route change, no-auto-listen-in-background. Runs in `chromium-voice-mic` **and** `desktop-webkit` (the real Safari/WKWebView engine the iOS PWA ships).
- `voice-pwa-bargein.spec.ts` — barge-in silences within budget, no-stale-audio-after-cancel invariant, double-tap idempotency (with a stability window so a late duplicate ASR POST cannot slip through green).
- `voice-pwa-framepump.spec.ts` — drives the REAL `AudioFramePump` (imported from `@elizaos/ui` source) with a captured `fetch`, pinning the 16 kHz / 20 ms / 320-sample batched-POST wire contract + size-cap mid-flush + terminal `flush:true`.
- `voice-pwa-failure-modes.spec.ts` — permission-denied visible state, hanging-provider time-bound (recovery requires leaving the active-listening label, not just an enabled button), transient-failure recovery.
- `voice-pwa-trace.spec.ts` — guarded consumer of #15931's `voice.*` completeness chain; green on current develop, load-bearing once #15931 lands; always writes the latency artifact.
- `voice-streaming-contract.spec.ts` — provider-agnostic streaming contract. The LLM lane drives the **real app stream client** (`ElizaClient.streamChatEndpoint`) over a chunked, time-spaced transport, so it catches an app parser that buffers the whole body; STT lane shims `SpeechRecognition` and **fails** (not skips) if the hook never starts it; TTS lane proves first-audio-before-last-token overlap via a chunked route + AudioContext probe.
- `playwright.ui-smoke.config.ts` — extends the existing `VOICE_MIC_SPEC` + `WEBKIT_SMOKE_SPECS` regexes only. **No new Playwright project, no new config file, no new harness** — reuses `chromium-voice-mic`, `desktop-webkit`, and default `chromium`.

## Design notes

- **WebKit/Chromium split (honest):** WebKit CI cannot honor Chromium's `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture`, so real-audio capture specs stay Chromium-mic-only; the lifecycle spec degrades to structural/engine assertions that DO run on the real Safari engine. WebKit proves *engine* behavior; Chromium-mic proves *audio-path* behavior. Neither is dropped.
- **Consumer-only relationship to #15931** (`sol/voice-trace-instrumentation-v2`): this lane asserts the trace contract #15931 emits; it touches none of #15931's files. `voice-pwa-trace` guards on mark presence (`test.skip` when absent) so it is merge-order-independent.
- **Collision check (re-verified against current open voice PRs):** zero overlap. #15946 (cloud WAV), #15931 (trace), #15927/#15929 (cloud), #15924 (shell mute-state), #15885/#15876/#15840/#15836 (transcript/PII/timestamps) — none own any `ui-smoke`/config file this lane creates or edits.

This check goes red because `packages/app/playwright.ui-smoke.config.ts` is counted as **changed source** by `scripts/security/coverage-changed-files.sh` (its `changed_source()` grep excludes `vitest.config.*` but **not** `playwright.*.config.ts`), while a Playwright config can never appear in a vitest LCOV report — so `coverage-gate.awk` fails it under enforcement with "changed source missing from LCOV".

There is no runtime source to cover. I added `packages/app/test/voice-pwa-latency-artifact.test.ts` (real vitest unit test for the pure `chainContainsInOrder` matcher) which clears the *"require changed tests for changed source"* leg, but the *LCOV-enforcement* leg still trips on the config file specifically.

Fix options for a maintainer (either is a one-liner, outside this tests-only lane's scope):
- add `playwright(\.[a-z-]+)?\.config\.(ts|js|mts|mjs|cts|cjs)$` to the `changed_source()` exclusion in `scripts/security/coverage-changed-files.sh` (mirrors the existing `vitest.config` exclusion), or
- treat the config change as non-source for this PR.

28:T1bab,Part of #14762, part of #14747

## Summary

Adds the **Signal Desktop corpus collector** (`packages/corpus-tools/src/collectors/signal.ts`) plus the shared collector infra the remaining collector lanes will reuse. This is the keyless code + fixture-test scope of #14762; the live decrypt on the owner's Mac (Keychain approval + real key) is the only owner-gated step and remains a gated evidence row.

What lands:

- **Key acquisition** (`signal-key.ts`) — resolves the SQLCipher key from `<Signal>/config.json`: plaintext `key` (legacy) or the Electron `safeStorage` `encryptedKey`, unwrapped in-process via the Chromium **OSCrypt v10** scheme (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 / `saltysalt` / 1003 iters / AES-128-CBC / all-spaces IV) keyed by the macOS Keychain item *"Signal Safe Storage"*. The Keychain read is an injected seam (`security find-generic-password` in production). The key is never persisted.
- **DB read** (`signal-db.ts`) — a `SignalDatabase` query seam and the production `openSqlcipherDatabase` adapter that applies `PRAGMA key` and probes before reading. The native cipher (`better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers`) is an **optional dependency** loaded dynamically and **fails closed** (`sqlcipher_unavailable`) when absent. The collector's SQL + normalization path is shared between production and tests (`createSignalDatabase` + one `SIGNAL_MESSAGE_QUERY`), so tests exercise it against a real SQLite engine without shipping the cipher.
- **Normalization** (`signal-normalize.ts`) — Signal row (json column authoritative, SQL columns as fallback) → `CorpusMessage`, with structural direction/sender/thread derivation. Body-less rows (reactions, attachment-only, membership events) and pre-cutoff rows are **skipped and counted, never fabricated into empty-text messages**.
- **Orchestrator** (`signal.ts`) — resolves the key, **copies** `db.sqlite` and reads the copy read-only (never the live DB), writes idempotent month shards, advances a `max(received_at)` resume checkpoint, and in `finally` **wipes the decrypted copy and asserts it is gone** (a failed wipe is a fail-closed error, not a warning).
- **Shared infra** — `checkpoint.ts` (atomic per-account resume markers, fail-closed on a corrupt marker) and `shard-writer.ts` (idempotent `<platform>/<account>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl` in the exact layout `validate` reads back), plus typed `CollectorError` (`errors.ts`). Reused by the other five collector lanes.
- **CLI** — `corpus collect signal` subcommand; typed exit codes (1 fail-closed, 2 usage).

Deviation from the issue's "commit an encrypted fixture DB": the tests **generate a real SQLite fixture with Signal's schema at test time** and inject a plaintext opener, so the whole query/normalization/shard/checkpoint/teardown path runs against a real query engine keyless — no opaque encrypted binary blob in git, and the only untested-locally step is the `PRAGMA key` decrypt itself, which is exactly the owner-gated part.

## Verification

2a:T2408,Fixes #15901, #15902, #15903 — the three onboarding defects isolated on a physical Pixel 6a during the #14358 Android close-out (evidence + logcat timelines: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/14358#issuecomment-4930960082). They share the client handoff surface and are fixed coherently here. **Do not merge without review — reviewer sign-off requested.**

## Root causes and fixes

### #15901 — handoff hard-fails during the proxy-route 404 window
**Root cause.** Control-plane `running` precedes actual routability: the runtime proxy can 404 the dedicated subdomain for minutes after the record flips (structural window, see the CP-side findings annotated on #15901 — the router only routes once `web_ui_port` + mesh IP register, and recovery is reactive). The client treated `status==="running" && url` as ready and did a **one-shot** import; the thrown 404 landed `phase: failed` seconds into a 10-minute budget → "Setup paused / Retry" for an agent that was actually coming up.
**Fix.**
- `resolveReadyBase` (`packages/ui/src/api/client-cloud.ts`) now probes the dedicated base itself (`GET /api/health`) and only reports ready once the proxy actually routes — 404/408/425/429/5xx or a network throw means "running but not yet routable", so the readiness poll keeps going inside its budget and the UI stays honestly in "Setting up…".
- `runConversationHandoff` (`packages/ui/src/cloud/handoff/conversation-handoff.ts`) retries transient step failures (`HandoffTransientError`: retryable HTTP statuses + network-layer throws, classified in `cloud-handoff-supervisor.ts`) by re-entering the readiness loop under **one shared deadline** — a step failure never re-arms a fresh budget, non-transient errors (401/403/…) still fail immediately, and an exhausted budget reports `timed-out`/`failed` honestly (user stays on the working shared adapter, Retry stays armed).
- CP-side "expose routable on the detail DTO" was investigated and deliberately not bundled (spans router daemon + CF Worker + SDK mirror); full findings + file map annotated on #15901.

### #15902 — stale `eliza:cloud-handoff-pending` marker pins "Setting up… / shared" forever
**Root cause.** The home provisioning tile rendered "Setting up…" for ANY shared-adapter session, forever, with nothing pending; a leftover marker from a previous (failed) onboarding also suppressed the fresh upgrade path in `bindCloudAgent`, and the marker was only reconciled on the boot-poll 404 path.
**Fix.**
- The widget (`agent-provisioning.tsx`) tracks a shared-adapter session only while a pending-handoff marker **for that agent** exists (the marker load TTL-clears expired entries); no marker + no live phase → render real state (nothing). A phase-event cache (`events/index.ts` + `useCloudHandoffPhase`) covers late mounts so an in-flight `migrating` is still visible.
- `bindCloudAgent` (`first-run-finish.ts`) clears a mismatched leftover marker, resumes a matching interrupted migration **at the landing** (`resumePendingCloudHandoff`, previously only reachable via the boot-poll 404 path), and never mints a second dedicated target for a reused agent that already owns one (`bridgeUrl` set).
- The dedicated-base boot landings in `startup-phase-poll.ts` also reconcile (a marker is provably stale once the active server is off the shared base).
- The Android spec's `resetKeys` now include `eliza:cloud-handoff-pending`.

### #15903 — `eliza:first-run-complete` never persisted on the returning-account landing
**Root cause.** Durable completion was persisted only through the conductor's React completion-callback chain; landing paths that bypass or outrun it (returning-account reuse, the pre-navigate pairing handoff that unloads the page) left the flag unset, so the next launch could re-enter first-run for a healthy agent.
**Fix.** Every successful cloud landing persists the flag **headlessly at the landing itself** in `bindCloudAgent` — fresh provision, returning-account reuse, in-process pairing, and before the `navigate` pairing hand-off — unified with (and idempotent to) the conductor's own `setFirstRunComplete(true)` persist.

2b:T1799,## What

Adds the **LP3-first ambient (always-listening) capture UI** for the Eliza app, built on top of the existing pendant session stack. Implements AMBIENT-MODE-DESIGN-2026-07-10 (consent, indicator, surfaces) + the VOICE-INTEGRATION-DECISION §7 contract.

**Flag-gated (`VITE_ENABLE_AMBIENT`), default OFF, zero behavior change when off.**

Signed: `[sol-cloud]` ambient-UI seat.

## Why

Ambient is "a second mode on the existing voice-session WebSocket" whose finals commit to the canonical `pendant_sessions_v1` store. The WS ambient mode is **not merged yet** (design §9, Phase 1a rides an in-flight server lane), so this lane delivers the user surface now, with the data layer behind a small adapter interface: the **batch path** (BLE mic → local VAD → local ASR → the existing pendant transcript store) is the working impl, and the **WS path is a documented TODO seam**. When the ambient WS mint + `stt_final`/`segment_committed` events land, only the adapter internals change — the UI is untouched.

## What's in it

**`packages/ui/src/ambient/` (new module)**
- `ambient-session-adapter.ts` — transport-agnostic adapter interface + status mapping + transport selection. `batch` working impl; `createAmbientWebSocketAdapter()` is the null seam for the not-yet-merged WS mode.
- `ambient-consent.ts` — per-session consent gate (not persisted; cleared on stop so each session re-prompts). Consent copy worded per processing path. Two-party bystander reminder (guidance, never a legal shield).
- `useAmbientSession.ts` — controller hook: enforces consent before start, folds pendant segments into the **reused** pendant transcript store, tracks session duration (excluding paused spans) + segment counts, resets bookkeeping + consent on stop.
- Components: **AmbientRecordingIndicator** (persistent, monochrome-safe: shape + motion + word, honest processing-location), **AmbientConsentGate**, **AmbientCaptureControl** (consent → start/pause/resume/stop + stats), **AmbientTranscriptFeed** (streaming pending/final segments, reused store).

**Surfaces**
- `components/pages/AmbientView.tsx` — the `/ambient` page.
- `components/settings/AmbientSettingsCard.tsx` — Settings → Voice entry point, mounted in `VoiceSection` behind the flag.
- Nav/route: `/ambient` registered in `TAB_PATHS`, `dev-route-catalog`, `view-routes`, and the aesthetic-audit parity table. The nav tile is flag-gated out of `ALL_TAB_GROUPS` when off, **and** the route mount is flag-gated in `App.tsx` so direct navigation to `/ambient` cannot open the always-listening surface when disabled.

## Design conformance

- **No new transcript / session / STT store or VAD** — reuses `pendant-transcript-session` + `usePendant` (design §11 forbidden-duplicates).
- **Consent enforced, not promised** (§8.1): no start without an explicit per-session grant.
- **Always-visible recording indicator** (§8.1): persistent bordered pill, communicates state via shape + motion + word (survives grayscale + reduced-motion), states processing-location honestly.
- **LP3 constraints** (§7.1): WebView 113-safe CSS (flex + border tokens, no bleeding-edge features), big tap targets (`size="lg"`, full-width buttons), grayscale-friendly.
- **Collision-free**: touches only new ambient components + settings additions. Did **not** touch `packages/ui/src/voice/*` (pwa-client lane) or `packages/ui/src/pendant/omi-protocol*/pendant-connection*` (pendant-stack lane).

## Codex review (gpt-5.5)

Ran and addressed 3 findings before opening:
1. Consent copy contradicted itself (hardcoded "cloud" while the batch path is on-device) → now worded per processing path via `ambientConsentAffirmation(location)`.

3. `/ambient` mounted even with the flag off (direct nav bypassed the gate) → route mount now flag-gated in `App.tsx` (renders the unavailable fallback when disabled).
